comment: The checks of a layer and the nesting rule (run 0093, wave 015, W-5; issues #90 and #87). LayerLoaderTest.java (command line) and layer-checks.test.js (editor) read this file; add a case here and both run it. `files`: a path from the folder of the workspace -> the text of the file (workspace.yaml is `settings: {manifests: {paths: [manifests/**]}}`); `plateau`: the plateau that is loaded (null: the workspace has no plateau, nothing is named). `cli`: what the command line does, which stops at the first layer that is wrong and draws nothing: `error` (the lines of its one `error:` message, in order) or `loaded` (the references of each layer it draws). `editor`: what the page does, which draws the plateau all the same so that it can be repaired, and tells the sentences of the first layer of the chain that is wrong: `problems` (null when there is none), `failedAt` (that plateau) and `drawn` (the references of the model, by layer). The sentences are the same in both tools. `nesting.holds`: which kinds a parent of each kind holds (a group holds what the element it sits in holds, and a leaf holds none), the sentence of K20 for every other pair; the model classes say it (`Nesting.java`, compared with this table by LayerLoaderTest), the page derives its tables from READ_SCHEMA (compared with this table by layer-checks.test.js), and each tool loads every pair of a parent and a child of the same layer, accepted or refused as this table says. Run 0093 also moves the case of #104 (an id with a dot) to plateau-model-cases.json, M81 to M83. Run 0100 (wave 015, W-12, issues #100 and #86) revises K04 and K05 and adds K32 to K36: a view and a story belong to no plateau, so what they name is not a mistake of a layer but a plateau-free check (every name exists in at least one plateau: it is declared by a manifest or by workspace.yaml, whatever the plateau). The command line tells it once, after the layers, and stops there; the editor tells it apart from the layers, whatever plateau is drawn (`entryProblems`, absent: none).
